title: Plastics
objective: After this level you can explain what plastic is made from and why it lasts so long.
summary: Plastics are long polymer chains, mostly from fossil-fuel carbon; Bakelite (1907) was the first fully synthetic one. Microbes can't digest them, so they break into microplastics.

cards.headline: Plastic got its start on the billiard table.
cards.body: In the 1860s, a billiards company offered a $10,000 prize for a substitute for ivory billiard balls. John Wesley Hyatt took up the challenge, and his work led to celluloid, one of the first plastics. What makes plastic so useful turns out to be what makes it so hard to get rid of.

cards.headline: Plastic is a very long chain
cards.body: Polymer means 'of many parts'. A plastic is made of long chains of small units repeated over and over, and the length of those chains makes it strong, light and flexible. Most plastics are built from carbon that comes from petroleum and other fossil fuels. In 1907, Leo Baekeland's Bakelite became the first fully synthetic plastic, made of no molecules found in nature.

cards.headline: Why nothing eats it
cards.body: Leaves and cardboard rot because microbes digest them, using enzymes to break the bonds in natural polymers such as lignin in plants. Those enzymes don't recognize the bonds that hold plastic together. So outdoors, plastic doesn't rot. It just breaks into smaller and smaller pieces, and it can take thousands of years to fully biodegrade. Being unnatural is exactly what makes it last.

cards.fact: Plastic pieces less than five millimeters long are called microplastics.
cards.context: That's about the size of a pencil eraser. Most plastic in the ocean breaks up into these small particles rather than disappearing. A bottle cap doesn't vanish; it turns into confetti.

questions.prompt: Level 13 traced crude oil to ancient marine life. What ties most plastics to those ancient creatures?

options.label: Plastics are made of ivory, like old billiard balls
options.rationale: Plastic was invented to replace ivory, not made from it.

options.label: Microbes digest both at the same slow rate
options.rationale: Microbes can't digest plastic at all.

options.label: Both formed under the seabed over millions of years
options.rationale: Plastic is made in factories from oil, not formed in rock.

questions.explanation: Most plastics are built from carbon supplied by petroleum and other fossil fuels, which formed from ancient sea life.
